newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa to undergo special heart test.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa to undergo special heart test.

text.p: Mother Teresa, in hospital with recurrent chest pain, has agreed to undergo a special X-ray test this week to see if an artery in her heart is blocked and an operation is needed, her doctor said on Tuesday.

Dr S.K. Sen of the Woodlands Nursing Home in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta said the 86-year-old nun would be moved to a nearby heart clinic for an angiography, an X-ray of blood vessels to see if she has a blocked artery.
Mother Teresa, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, has twice undergone coronary angiography -- once in 1991 in the United States and a second time in 1993 in Calcutta.
In both cases she subsequently underwent angioplasty, in which surgeons inserted a balloon into her artery to unblock it.
Woodlands Nursing Home said in a medical bulletin that the results of the angiography would determine whether she needed angioplasty.

Sen told reporters that Mother Teresa would be moved to Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre on Tuesday afternoon for the angiography. The procedure would probably be carried out on Wednesday, he said.
Dr Patricia Aubanel, who treated her in the United States, has arrived in Calcutta to help supervise the procedure, he said.
Known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the world's downtrodden, the 86-year-old nun was admitted to hospital with an irregular heart beat early on Friday.

Mother Teresa, who has ischaemia, or hardening of the arteries, has suffered heart failure three times since last Thursday. But on Monday she had shown some reluctance to undergo any special tests or surgery.
Sen was asked how he convinced Mother Teresa to undergo the special X-ray.

"I said, 'Look, you have been having this problem and we all think that this is because of blockage of the artery. If not taken care of now, it may lead to heart attack. Angioplasty is preventive care, so why don't you accept?'"
Mother Teresa then asked him, "How long are you going to keep me in hospital?" Sen said seven days, and she agreed.

The doctor said angioplasty was a very safe procedure involving the injection of dye through a catheter. The dye shows up on the X-ray, revealing any blockage. She will be put under general anaesthesia, Sen said.
Earlier on Tuesday, Mother Teresa's cardiologist said her persistent irregular heart beat was worrying, but that she was reluctant to undergo surgery.
"When she agreed, we decided to do it quickly unless she might change her decision," Sen said.
Sen said an alternative to angioplasty would be cardioversion, involving electric shock. "Last time she vehemently refused to accept cardioversion," he said.
The two doctors who performed angioplasty on Mother Teresa at the Birla centre in 1993, Dr Deepak Shetty and Dr Tarun Praharaj, will conduct the angiography, Sen said.

Since being fitted with the heart pacemaker, Mother Teresa has spent time in hospital for heart disease, bacterial pneumonia, broken ribs, malaria and lung problems. When she was rushed to Woodlands Nursing Home last week, it was the third time since last August that she had been admitted for emergency care.
